title: Tails, You Win
coreMove: Arrange your behavior so rare big winners can matter while ordinary misses stay survivable.
sourcePressure: In lumpy systems, a few outsized outcomes drive most results, so average stretches and many misses are part of the structure.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Assuming every choice must work or the strategy is broken.

hook: opening with a generic paycheck scene
opening with a moral lesson about discipline
opening Tails, You Win with a swapped-in personal finance anecdote
counterintuition: reducing Tails, You Win to common-sense advice
tryThisNow: write down your values for ninety seconds
asking for a generic money reflection instead of the tail events move
examples: reusing visible anchors from adjacent chapters instead of tail events and outsized wins

exampleSpecs.domain: an independent record label funding ten small artists knowing one breakout keeps the label alive
exampleSpecs.audience: a label manager accepting misses as structure rather than failure
exampleSpecs.stakes: cutting slow acts too early may eliminate the future catalog winner
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager marks which past revenue came from two tracks nobody predicted before setting the new roster budget
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a royalty spreadsheet with two rows highlighted in yellow

exampleSpecs.domain: a venture philanthropy fund backing many clean-water pilots
exampleSpecs.audience: a program officer explaining why most pilots can be mediocre if one scales cleanly
exampleSpecs.stakes: overreacting to average pilots would kill the outlier that changes thousands of wells
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she keeps funding breadth after isolating the one village pilot with repeatable maintenance behavior
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a field report packet stained by rain at the corners

exampleSpecs.domain: a fishing fleet experimenting with several grounds during a strange migration season
exampleSpecs.audience: a captain teaching crew that empty hauls can be the cost of finding the one heavy run
exampleSpecs.stakes: abandoning exploration too soon misses the season's tail catch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain plots nine poor hauls and the one hold-filling haul on the same chart before changing strategy
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a marine chart with pencil X marks across open water

exampleSpecs.domain: a children's publisher accepting many modest titles because one perennial pays for the list
exampleSpecs.audience: an editor defending a portfolio to finance staff
exampleSpecs.stakes: measuring every manuscript by immediate sales misunderstands the business
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the editor pulls ten years of backlist sales and shows the one quiet title still carrying payroll
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a shelf of thin picture-book galleys beside a backlist report

exampleSpecs.domain: a disaster-response warehouse stocking many items rarely used so the one needed item is present
exampleSpecs.audience: a logistics lead explaining unused inventory to auditors
exampleSpecs.stakes: efficiency metrics may remove the exact supply that matters in a rare crisis
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a flood, she shows that one obscure pump adapter made the whole warehouse worthwhile
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a metal adapter tagged with mud from the flood site

exampleSpecs.domain: a long-term index investor reviewing years where a few days explain most gains
exampleSpecs.audience: a saver tempted to leave after dull returns
exampleSpecs.stakes: missing the handful of surge days damages the whole plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he covers the top five trading days on the chart and watches the long-term line flatten
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a return chart with removable notes covering five dates
